t: In which year was the Accounting Standards Board (ASB) constituted in India?
e: The ASB was set up in 1977 and is responsible for formulating accounting standards in India.

t: The Accounting Standards Board that formulates Ind AS functions under which body?
o: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI)
e: Ind AS are developed under the supervision of the ASB of ICAI, in consultation with NFRA.

t: Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) are harmonised with which international framework?
o: UK GAAP issued by the FRC
US GAAP issued by the FASB
e: Ind AS are converged with the International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) of the IASB to improve global comparability.

t: According to the trainer's material, how many Accounting Standards has ICAI issued so far?
e: The material states that ICAI has come out with 32 standards so far, of which AS 1 to AS 29 are listed.

t: AS 29 deals with which subject?
o: Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets
e: AS 29 covers provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets; AS 28 is impairment, AS 26 intangibles and AS 19 leases.

t: Which Accounting Standard is specifically NOT applicable to insurers carrying on general insurance business?
e: AS 13 does not apply to insurers because IRDAI prescribes its own procedure for valuation of investments.

t: Which of the following is NOT one of the five basic accounting principles listed in the material?
e: The five basic principles listed are accrual, conservatism, economic entity, consistency and going concern.

t: A divisional office trial balance shows total assets of ₹850 lakh and total liabilities of ₹620 lakh. Using the accounting equation, the capital is:
e: Capital = Assets − Liabilities = ₹850 lakh − ₹620 lakh = ₹230 lakh.

t: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) is governed by which section of the Companies Act, 2013?
e: Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 deals with CSR; 138 is internal audit, 149 Board of Directors and 177 Audit Committee.

t: Appointment of auditors of a Government company is dealt with under which provision of the Companies Act, 2013?
e: Section 139(7) covers auditor appointment for companies owned or controlled by the Central or State Government, where the CAG appoints the auditor.

t: If capital is ₹300 crore and liabilities are ₹1,700 crore, total assets as per the accounting equation are:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Assets = Capital + Liabilities = 300 + 1,700 = ₹2,000 crore.

t: DTL in accounting terminology refers to:
e: DTL means Deferred Tax Liability, the counterpart of DTA (Deferred Tax Asset).

t: Cash book shows a favourable balance of ₹5,00,000. Cheques issued but not presented ₹1,20,000; cheques deposited but not yet credited ₹80,000; bank charges debited by bank not recorded in cash book ₹2,000. Balance as per pass book is:
International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) are issued by:
o: Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI)
e: IFRS are issued by the IASB with the objective of providing a common accounting language.

t: MCA made adoption of Ind AS mandatory for all listed companies and certain others from which financial year?
e: In 2015 the MCA mandated Ind AS for listed companies and a few others with effect from FY 2016-17.

t: Ind AS 117 'Insurance Contracts' aligns with which international standard?
e: Ind AS 117 is the Indian counterpart of IFRS 17, which deals with insurance and reinsurance contracts.

t: Under the IRDAI (Actuarial, Finance and Investment Functions of Insurers) Regulations, 2024, loans and advances by insurance companies are covered in:
e: Schedule I is actuarial, II finance, III investment, IV loans and advances, and V inspection and supply of returns.

t: Gross Direct Premium, as defined, specifically excludes:
o: GST element and premium received in advance
e: Gross Direct Premium is premium booked directly from policyholders for the accounting year excluding GST and premium received in advance.

t: An insurer books gross direct premium of ₹1,200 crore, accepts reinsurance inward of ₹100 crore and cedes ₹300 crore. Net Written Premium is:
e: GWP = 1,200 + 100 = ₹1,300 crore; Net Premium = GWP − ceded = 1,300 − 300 = ₹1,000 crore.

t: Gross claims paid ₹500 crore and reinsurance recoveries on claims ₹120 crore. Net claims paid are:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Net claims = gross claims less reinsurance recoveries = 500 − 120 = ₹380 crore.

t: Net Written Premium is ₹1,000 crore, opening Unearned Premium Reserve ₹450 crore and closing UPR ₹520 crore. Net Earned Premium is:
e: NEP = NWP − (closing UPR − opening UPR) = 1,000 − 70 = ₹930 crore.

t: Gross claims paid during the year ₹600 crore; gross outstanding claims (including IBNR) at year end ₹900 crore and at the beginning ₹820 crore. Gross Incurred Claims are:
e: Gross incurred = paid + closing outstanding − opening outstanding = 600 + 900 − 820 = ₹680 crore.

t: A reserve reflecting expected changes in the estimates of claims already reported (including ALAE) is called:
e: IBNER (Incurred But Not Enough Reported) reserves cover expected development in estimates of reported claims.

t: As per the material, the IBNR reserve includes provision for:
o: Only claims that have not been reported at all
Claims in transit, ALAE and an estimate for reopened claims
e: IBNR covers incurred but not reported claims, claims in transit as on the valuation date, ALAE and reopened claims.

t: Reserve for Unexpired Risks (URR) is determined as the aggregate of:
o: Unearned Premium Reserve and Premium Deficiency Reserve
e: URR = UPR + PDR as per the definitions in the IRDAI regulations.

t: For a segment the UPR is ₹400 crore. Expected claim costs are ₹350 crore and related expenses and maintenance costs ₹70 crore. The Premium Deficiency Reserve to be recognised is:
e: Expected costs 350 + 70 = ₹420 crore exceed the UPR of ₹400 crore, so a PDR of ₹20 crore is recognised.

t: For solvency margin computation, agents' and intermediaries' balances and outstanding premiums in India are valued at zero to the extent not realised within:
e: Agents' balances and outstanding premium in India not realised within 30 days are placed at zero value.

t: Net Written Premium ₹2,400 crore; opening UPR ₹1,300 crore; closing UPR ₹1,200 crore. Net Earned Premium is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). A release of UPR adds to earned premium: 2,400 − (1,200 − 1,300) = ₹2,500 crore.

t: A co-insurance balance receivable from the leader is outstanding for 100 days as on the balance sheet date. For solvency purposes it is:
o: Valued at zero, as co-insurer balances beyond 90 days are inadmissible
e: Co-insurers' balances outstanding for more than 90 days are placed at zero value for solvency computation.

t: An insurer carries a Deferred Tax Asset of ₹40 crore, none of which arises from accumulated losses. For solvency computation the admissible value is:
e: 75% of DTA not arising from accumulated losses is placed at zero, so only 25% × 40 = ₹10 crore is admissible.

t: RSM 1 is computed as:
o: 20% of the higher of Gross Premium × Factor A and Net Premium
30% of the higher of Gross Premium × Factor A and Net Premium
e: RSM 1 (premium basis) is 20% of the higher of gross premium multiplied by Factor A and net premium.

t: For a line of business, Gross Premium × Factor A = ₹900 crore, Net Premium ₹800 crore, Gross Incurred Claims × Factor B = ₹500 crore and Net Incurred Claims ₹560 crore. The Required Solvency Margin is:
e: RSM1 = 20% × 900 = 180; RSM2 = 30% × 560 = 168; RSM is the higher, ₹180 crore.

t: Available Solvency Margin is ₹2,700 crore and Required Solvency Margin ₹1,500 crore. The solvency ratio is:
e: Solvency ratio = ASM / RSM = 2,700 / 1,500 = 1.80.

topic: Supplement: Insurance Act and IRDAI Rules
t: The control level of solvency that every insurer must maintain at all times under IRDAI norms is:
e: IRDAI requires a minimum solvency ratio of 1.50, i.e. ASM must be at least 150% of RSM.

t: AS 3 classifies cash flows during a period under which three heads?
e: The cash flow statement classifies flows into operating, investing and financing activities.

t: Non-disclosure of a material fact by the proposer makes the contract:
o: Voidable at the option of the insurer
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Breach of utmost good faith renders the contract voidable, not void; the insurer may elect to avoid it (subject to Section 45 for life).

t: Net written premium during the preceding twelve months: Marine Hull ₹50 crore and Fire ₹300 crore. Using the percentage method, total Unearned Premium Reserve is:
e: Marine Hull 100% × 50 = 50; Fire 50% × 300 = 150; total UPR ₹200 crore.

t: The CFO wishes to switch from the 50% method to the 1/365 (unexpired period) method of providing UPR. What is required?
o: No approval, as both methods are permitted
Prior written approval of the Competent Authority
e: Any change in the method of provisioning for UPR requires prior written approval of the Competent Authority.

t: Listed equity shares costing ₹120 crore have a fair value of ₹150 crore on the balance sheet date. The ₹30 crore difference is:
o: Credited to the Fair Value Change Account under equity
Credited to the Profit and Loss Account
e: Unrealised gains or losses on actively traded equity are taken to the Fair Value Change Account, not to profit.

t: Figures in the financial statements of an insurer may be rounded off to the nearest:
e: The general instructions permit rounding off figures to the nearest lakhs.

t: Income tax deducted at source on interest and dividend receivable on investments (accounted gross) is shown under:
e: TDS on investment income accounted on gross basis is included under advance taxes paid.

t: The Revenue Account (Policyholders' Account) of a general insurer is prepared in:
e: Form B-RA is the Revenue Account, B-PL the Profit and Loss Account and B-BS the Balance Sheet.

t: Deduction for life insurance premium under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act is available up to an overall limit of:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). ₹1,50,000 aggregate for all 80C items; premium qualifies only up to 10% of the sum assured for policies issued after 1 April 2012.

t: An insurer's gross direct premium is ₹2,000 crore, of which Marine Cargo contributes ₹230 crore. Is a separate segment schedule required for Marine Cargo?
o: No, because only the listed segments need separate schedules
Yes, because it contributes 11.5%, more than 10% of gross direct premium
Yes, because every segment above ₹100 crore is shown separately
e: Any other sub-segment contributing more than 10% of total gross direct premium must be shown separately; 230/2,000 = 11.5%.

t: Share capital ₹200 crore; reserves and surplus ₹800 crore (including Revaluation Reserve ₹50 crore and Fair Value Change Account ₹30 crore); miscellaneous expenditure not written off ₹10 crore. Shareholders' Funds are:
e: Shareholders' funds exclude revaluation reserve and FVCA and are net of misc. expenditure: 200 + 800 − 50 − 30 − 10 = ₹910 crore.

t: The aggregate of all loans to a full-time employee of an insurer shall not exceed:
e: Aggregate loans to an employee are capped at rupees one crore and linked to fixed remuneration.

t: The minimum paid-up equity capital for a company carrying on exclusively reinsurance business is:
e: Reinsurers need ₹200 crore; life, general and standalone health insurers need ₹100 crore.

t: In the order of seniority of claims on an insurer, which class ranks first?
e: The order is policyholders, creditors, subordinated debt holders, preference shareholders and lastly equity shareholders.

t: Gross premium written in India is ₹5,000 crore and incremental premium from PMFBY is ₹200 crore. The allowable expenses of management are:
e: 30% × 5,000 = 1,500 plus 15% of incremental PMFBY premium 200 = 30; total ₹1,530 crore.

t: Net incurred claims ₹780 crore, net earned premium ₹1,000 crore, expenses of management including net commission ₹250 crore and net written premium ₹1,050 crore. The combined ratio is approximately:
e: Combined ratio = 780/1,000 (78%) + 250/1,050 (23.8%) = 101.8%, indicating an underwriting loss.
